Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_figma flows; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use-figjam/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-diagram — MANDATORY before calling generate_diagram; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md
- /figma-design-to-code — MANDATORY before calling get_design_context; fallback: skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → FigJam file, use get_figjam
- figma.com/slides/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Slides file

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW (Figma → code):
MANDATORY: load the /figma-design-to-code skill BEFORE calling get_design_context — it carries the full workflow (adapting the reference, reusing existing project components and tokens, and honoring the response's hints by priority). Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey — it is your primary tool; its output is a REFERENCE to adapt to the target project, not final code.

CODE-TO-DESIGN WORKFLOW (code → Figma):
1. Load the /figma-generate-design skill if available.
2. ALWAYS call search_design_system first to find existing components, variables, and styles to reuse — never generate components from scratch if a design system match exists.
3. For web app pages, use both tools in parallel: generate_figma_design to capture a pixel-perfect screenshot, and use_figma to build the screen from imported design system components. Refine use_figma output against the screenshot, then delete the screenshot reference.
4. For non-web targets (iOS, Android, generic UI), use use_figma with search_design_system.
5. For updating or syncing a Figma page that has already been captured, use use_figma — even if the source code has changed.

FROM-SCRATCH DESIGN WORKFLOW (no source design or code):

1	import express = require('express')
2	import Path = require('path')
3	
4	import Logger = require('../Logger')
5	import SocketAuthority = require('../SocketAuthority')
6	
7	import fs = require('../libs/fsExtra')
8	type Auth = import('../Auth')
9	type PlaybackSessionManager = import('../managers/PlaybackSessionManager')
10	
11	
12	class HlsRouter {
13	  declare auth: Auth
14	  declare playbackSessionManager: PlaybackSessionManager
15	  declare router: express.Express
16	
17	  constructor(auth: Auth, playbackSessionManager: PlaybackSessionManager) {
18	    this.auth = auth
19	    this.playbackSessionManager = playbackSessionManager
20	
21	    this.router = express()
22	    this.router.disable('x-powered-by')
23	    this.init()
24	  }
25	
26	  init(): void {
27	    this.router.get('/:stream/:file', this.streamFileRequest.bind(this))
28	  }
29	
30	  parseSegmentFilename(filename: string): number {
31	    var basename = Path.basename(filename, Path.extname(filename))
32	    var num_part = basename.split('-')[1]
33	    return Number(num_part)
34	  }
35	
36	  /**
37	   * Ensure filepath is inside streamDir
38	   * Used to prevent arbitrary file reads
39	   * @see https://nodejs.org/api/path.html#pathrelativefrom-to
40	   * 
41	   * @param {string} streamDir 
42	   * @param {string} filepath 
43	   * @returns {boolean}
44	   */
45	  validateStreamFilePath(streamDir: string, filepath: string): string | boolean {
46	    const relative = Path.relative(streamDir, filepath)
47	    return relative && !relative.startsWith('..') && !Path.isAbsolute(relative)
48	  }
49	
50	  /**
51	   * GET /hls/:stream/:file
52	   * File must have extname .ts or .m3u8
53	   * 
54	   * @param {express.Request} req 
55	   * @param {express.Response} res 
56	   */
57	  async streamFileRequest(req: express.Request, res: express.Response): Promise<express.Response | undefined> {
58	    const streamId = req.params.stream
59	    // Ensure stream is open
60	    const stream = this.playbackSessionManager.getStream(streamId)
61	    if (!stream) {
62	      Logger.error(`[HlsRouter] Stream "${streamId}" does not exist`)
63	      return res.sendStatus(404)
64	    }
65	
66	    // Ensure stream filepath is valid
67	    const streamDir = Path.join(this.playbackSessionManager.StreamsPath, streamId)
68	    const fullFilePath = Path.join(streamDir, req.params.file)
69	    if (!this.validateStreamFilePath(streamDir, fullFilePath)) {
70	      Logger.error(`[HlsRouter] Invalid file parameter "${req.params.file}"`)
71	      return res.sendStatus(400)
72	    }
73	
74	    const fileExt = Path.extname(req.params.file)
75	    if (fileExt !== '.ts' && fileExt !== '.m3u8') {
76	      Logger.error(`[HlsRouter] Invalid file parameter "${req.params.file}" extname. Must be .ts or .m3u8`)
77	      return res.sendStatus(400)
78	    }
79	
80	    if (!(await fs.pathExists(fullFilePath))) {
81	      Logger.warn('File path does not exist', fullFilePath)
82	
83	      if (fileExt === '.ts') {
84	        const segNum = this.parseSegmentFilename(req.params.file)
85	
86	        if (stream.isResetting) {
87	          Logger.info(`[HlsRouter] Stream ${streamId} is currently resetting`)
88	        } else {
89	          const startTimeForReset = await stream.checkSegmentNumberRequest(segNum)
90	          if (startTimeForReset) {
91	            // HLS.js will restart the stream at the new time
92	            Logger.info(`[HlsRouter] Resetting Stream - notify client @${startTimeForReset}s`)
93	            SocketAuthority.emitter('stream_reset', {
94	              startTime: startTimeForReset,
95	              streamId: stream.id
96	            })
97	          }
98	        }
99	      }
100	      return res.sendStatus(404)
101	    }
102	
103	    res.sendFile(fullFilePath)
104	  }
105	}
106	export = HlsRouter

## Sub-agent 1 report (PO-S08)

All nine controllers are converted and type-check clean. One decision is yours: the two casts in `ApiKeyController.ts` are not literally covered by any CLAUDE.md allowance (details under "Casts").

Stopped at **05:04:27** by `date`. Final filtered `npx tsc -p tsconfig.check.json` output for my nine files: **empty** (grep exit 1). The unfiltered output at that moment had 2 lines, both in `ShareController.ts` (not mine).

I did not run the build or the tests, and I did not use git add or commit. `git status` shows only the nine renames (`RM`) for my set; nothing outside `server/controllers/` is touched.

### Per controller

| Controller | Status | `!` | Index sig. | A1 | A2 | A3 | Other casts | `this: ApiRouter` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stats | converted | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| CustomMetadataProvider | converted | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Email | converted | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 2 |

Non-null assertion: `NotificationController.ts:111`, `req.notification.id!` (rule 5). `Notification.id` is `string | null` and `removeNotification(id: string)` takes a string.

### Casts (all "other", each with a one-line comment)

- **`EmailController.ts:131`**: `libraryItem.media.ebookFile as Book['ebookFile'] | undefined`. Rule 5 boundary cast. LibraryItem.js types `media` as book or podcast, and the index signature in `Podcast.ts` (line 67) makes `media.ebookFile` `unknown`. Without the cast: `TS2345: Argument of type '{}' is not assignable to parameter of type 'EbookFileToSend'`.
- **`FileSystemController.ts:160`**: `(Database.libraryItemModel as LibraryItemFindOne).findOne(...)`. Rule 5 boundary cast. `LibraryItemFindOne` is a local type with only `findOne`. Without the cast: `TS2769 ... The 'this' context of type 'typeof LibraryItem' is not assignable to method's 'this' of type 'ModelStatic<LibraryItem>' ... Types of property 'init' are incompatible`.
- **`BackupController.ts:129`**: `(fs as typeof fs & { mkdir(path: string): Promise<void> }).mkdir(...)`. This is the fsExtra allowance in "Pitfalls". Without the cast: `TS2551: Property 'mkdir' does not exist`.
- **`ToolsController.ts:85`**: `getPendingTaskByLibraryItemId(req.params.id) as { task: Task } | null`. Rule 5 boundary cast. AbMergeManager.js documents `Task|null` but returns the pending entry `{ id, task }`. Without the cast, `workerTask.task` is `TS2339: Property 'task' does not exist on type 'Task'` (confirmed with a scratchpad probe).
- **`ApiKeyController.ts:106` and `:175`**: `(apiKeyInstance as ApiKeyWithGetUser).getUser(...)` and `(apiKey as ApiKeyWithGetUser).getUser(...)`. **Not literally covered.** The converted `ApiKey.ts` does not declare the `getUser` mixin that `ApiKey.belongsTo(user)` adds (`TS2339: Property 'getUser' does not exist on type 'ApiKey'`, confirmed with a probe). Your options for ApiKey:
1. Accept the two casts.
2. Add this line to `ApiKey.ts`, plus `BelongsToGetAssociationMixin` in its sequelize type import: `declare getUser: BelongsToGetAssociationMixin<User> // mixin added by ApiKey.belongsTo(user) in init(); ApiKeyController calls it`. Then in `ApiKeyController.ts` remove line 3, lines 14–15, the comment lines 105 and 174, and turn lines 106 and 175 back into `apiKeyInstance.getUser({` and `apiKey.getUser({`.
3. Restore the file: `git mv server/controllers/ApiKeyController.ts server/controllers/ApiKeyController.js` then `git restore server/controllers/ApiKeyController.js`.

### Annotated destructured imports

- `FileSystemController.ts`: `../utils/index`, `toNumber: (val: unknown, fallback?: number) => number` (inferred was `(val: any, ...)`).
- `CustomMetadataProviderController.ts`: `../utils/index`, `validateUrl: (rawUrl: string) => string | null` (the JSDoc says `string`, but it returns null for an invalid url).

### Declarations needed in server/types/

None. `ApiKeyController.ts` uses the existing `uuid` declaration through `/// <reference path="../types/untypedModules.d.ts" />`, written as in `Notification.ts` (`import uuid = require('uuid')`, then `const uuidv4 = uuid.v4`).

### For the commit message

- `import type { NextFunction, Request, Response } from 'express'` replaces a require of names that are undefined at runtime in all nine files (FileSystemController had only `Request, Response`).
- New type-only imports that replace nothing: `FindOptions` from sequelize (FileSystem) and `BelongsToGetAssociationMixin` from sequelize (ApiKey).

### Problems in ApiRouter.js, converted files and JS files I call

- `server/models/ApiKey.ts`: no `declare getUser` (mixin from `belongsTo(user)`, line 287). I cast at the two call sites, as above.
- `server/models/LibraryItem.js` (still JS): its `static init(sequelize)` makes every inherited Sequelize static (`findOne`, `findByPk`, `findAll`, `count`, ...) uncallable from TypeScript. Custom statics such as `getExpandedById` work. A cast to `ModelStatic<LibraryItem>` is rejected with TS2352; a cast to a small local type with only the static used is accepted. Other controllers will hit this.
- `server/models/Podcast.ts:67`: the class index signature makes any property read on a `Book | Podcast` media union `unknown`. I cast in EmailController.
- `server/objects/Notification.ts`: `id: string | null` forces the `!` in NotificationController.
- `server/managers/AbMergeManager.js:23,30`: the JSDoc says `Task[]` and `Task|null`, but the entries are `{ id, task }` and `find()` returns undefined. I cast in ToolsController. TypeScript accepts `as { task: Task } | null` only because both unions share `null`; `| undefined` gives TS2352.
- `server/managers/AbMergeManager.js:12-17`: `AbMergeEncodeOptions` marks `codec`, `channels` and `bitrate` as required. To avoid a cast I typed the encode-m4b query as the callee's own parameter type (`EncodeQuery`), so the query type claims all three are present.
- `server/routers/ApiRouter.js:57`: `this.apiCacheManager` has no JSDoc type, so it is `any`. `BackupController.apply` passes it on unchecked. Nothing done.
- `server/managers/BackupManager.js`: `backups` is `any[]` and `uploadBackup(req, res)` is untyped, so `req.backup = ...find(...)` and the upload call are unchecked. Nothing done.

### Bug log (line numbers of the original .js at HEAD; nothing fixed)

1. `BackupController.js:71`: `req.files.file` is read without a guard on `req.files`, so an upload request that is not multipart throws a TypeError instead of reaching the handler's own "invalid" response.
2. `NotificationController.js:106-107`: `updateNotification` ignores the `:id` in the URL and looks the notification up by `req.body.id`, so another notification, or none, can be updated while the response is still 200.
3. `NotificationController.js:79-84`: `createNotification` answers 200 with the settings even when the payload is rejected. A body without `urls` throws in `NotificationSettings.ts:129` (`payload.urls.length`).
4. `ToolsController.js:70`: `cancelEncode()` returns a promise (`removeTask` is async) that is neither awaited nor caught; 200 is sent before the task is removed.
5. `ToolsController.js:31,36,41,46,161`: log messages name `[MiscController]` and `[LibraryItemController]`; line 161 also says "Non-root" although the check is `isAdminOrUp`.
6. `ToolsController.js:113`: `libraryItemIds` is not checked to be an array; a string is iterated by character, and a non-iterable object with a `length` throws.
7. `FileSystemController.js:30-34`: `req.query.path` is assumed to be a string; `?path=a&path=b` gives an array and `Path.isAbsolute` throws instead of the 400 response.
8. `ApiKeyController.js:179-189` (possible): `delete` has no root check, so a non-root admin can delete a root user's API key, while `create` (68) and `update` (122) refuse to act on root keys.
9. `ApiKeyController.js:139`: the log message in `update` says "cannot be created" (copied from `create`).
10. `CustomMetadataProviderController.js:45-54` (possible): `validUrl` is only tested; the raw `url` is stored, not the normalised one.
11. `RSSFeedController.js:157`: passes `req.body` where the two sibling handlers pass `reqBody` (same object at that point; inconsistency only).
12. `EmailController.js:135` (possible): `adminMiddleware` answers 404 for a non-admin where the other controllers answer 403.
13. `StatsController.js:53`: the log prints the converted value (`NaN`), not the raw `req.params.year`.

### CLAUDE.md: what did not work as written or was not covered

- No disagreement between your brief and CLAUDE.md.
- Not covered: inherited Sequelize statics on the still-JavaScript LibraryItem model.
- Not covered: an association mixin that a converted model does not declare (ApiKey `getUser`).
- Not covered: a JS manager reached through `this` (not a destructured import) whose JSDoc return type is wrong. "Annotate the destructured import" has nothing to annotate, so I used a rule 5 cast.
- Not covered: a JS callee whose JSDoc parameter type is too narrow. Allowance 3 names only already converted files. I derived the request type from the callee's parameter instead of casting.
- "Use the generics of Request once per controller": where handlers have different bodies or params I wrote `Request<...>` once in a generic alias with defaults, keeping the JSDoc name (`RequestWithUser<Body = unknown>` in Email and Notification, `RequestWithUser<Params>` in RSSFeed and Tools). Tell me if you want one flat type per controller instead.
- The plain `Request & { user: User }` form of `CacheController.ts` leaves `req.body` as `any` (the @types/express default). I used the generics wherever a body is read; `StatsController.ts` keeps the plain form because it reads no body or query.
- The grep in the check command shows only the first line of a multi-line error; `grep -A12` shows the cause.
- The "Debug Failure" crash did not occur in the no-emit check.

### Files (all in `D:\SEM-2\574\Project\audiobookshelf-po\server\controllers\`)

- `StatsController.ts`
- `CustomMetadataProviderController.ts`
- `EmailController.ts`
- `NotificationController.ts`
- `FileSystemController.ts`
- `BackupController.ts`
- `ToolsController.ts`
- `RSSFeedController.ts`
- `ApiKeyController.ts`
